_about: The cross-reference index of the teachings. Read docs/cross-reference.md first. Concepts, page status and findings are kept by hand; fingerprints are stamped by scripts/check-content-index.py --record after the changed pages have been re-read against the index; mentions are worked out from the terms on every run.

Hinduism.note: "That thou art". Identity of self and ultimate reality is one school's reading of three.

Islam.note: The oneness of God, and God as the Light of the heavens and the earth.

Christianity.note: "You are the light of the world" and "God is light" are different sayings with different subjects.

Sikhism.note: One creator, and the Lord's Light within all.

Seicho-no-Ie.note: Only the perfect world God created truly exists.

Islam.note: Prayer, fasting and pilgrimage among the five.

Hinduism.note: Paths of action, knowledge and devotion for different temperaments. The fourfold scheme is modern (S58).

Buddhism.note: The eightfold path; mindfulness of breathing as a path to liberation.

Christianity.note: Giving, prayer and fasting, done in secret.

Islam.note: Zakat, an obligation, and not only relief of the poor.

Christianity.note: The least of these; the merciful and the peacemakers.

Hinduism.note: Non-injury as a virtue. Not general pacifism.

Buddhism.note: Right speech and action; the five precepts.

Sikhism.note: Work for what you eat and give some of what you have.

Islam.note: The word and the teaching as the page uses it. Cite the verse; the hadith (S90) names other traditions.

Judaism.note: Made in the image of God.

Seicho-no-Ie.note: Already perfect, a child of God.

Buddhism.note: Buddha-nature is a Mahayana teaching of the potential for awakening, contested within Mahayana, and not the goodness of a soul. Needs a further source.

Judaism.note: Love your neighbour, read with love the stranger; Hillel's rule, quoted whole.

Christianity.note: Jesus quotes Leviticus; the Samaritan widens the neighbour; love of enemies.

Islam.note: Against those who drive away the orphan; the merciful are shown mercy.

Buddhism.note: The Huayan school's net of Indra and Thich Nhat Hanh's interbeing. Early dependent origination (S74) explains the arising of suffering and only resembles this.

Hinduism.note: The whole world as a family: a late text about a detached sage.

Indigenous traditions.note: Māori kaitiakitanga; the Haudenosaunee Thanksgiving Address. Each is that people's own, not a general ethic.

Hawaiian tradition.note: Aloha ʻāina and mālama ʻāina, political as well as ecological.

Seicho-no-Ie.note: Grand Harmony of God, Nature, and Human Beings.

learning.label: Pursuit of knowledge and continuous learning

Islam.note: "My Lord, increase me in knowledge". The well-known hadith (S94) has a very weak chain.

Judaism.note: Study, and dispute for the sake of Heaven.

Buddhism.note: Test a teaching by its fruits and by what the wise praise. Not a licence to believe what one likes.

world-traditions.label: Respect for the wisdom of world traditions

Seicho-no-Ie.note: All religions emanate from one universal God. The nearest statement of UPL's own premise.

Islam.note: One community, said after a list of earlier prophets. Translations differ.

Hinduism.note: "To what is One, sages give many a title" names Vedic gods. Reading it as a statement about all religions is modern.

Buddhism.note: The teaching as a raft, a means and not an end. It is about the Buddha's own teaching, not about other religions.

Islam.note: Successors upon the earth, often understood as stewardship; do not be excessive.

Judaism.note: Do not destroy: a rabbinic extension of a verse on fruit trees. The environmental reading is modern.

Christianity.note: Francis of Assisi, patron of those who promote ecology; the Canticle of the Creatures.

Buddhism.note: The Sangha: in the early texts the monastic order or the community of the awakened.

Christianity.note: Washing one another's feet; whoever would be great shall serve.

Sikhism.note: The shared meal open to all, and seva. Traditionally traced to Guru Nanak.

Seicho-no-Ie.note: The law of the mind: thought, word and deed shape the phenomenal world.

Islam.note: Gratitude, which is sourced. The page also credits Islam with positive conduct and mindful awareness, for which no source is recorded yet.

Buddhism.note: Mind or intention comes first, leading speech and action. It does not say thoughts create reality.

Christianity.note: Do not be anxious: trust, turning on "seek first God's Kingdom", not the power of thought.

Indigenous traditions.note: Thanks to each part of the natural world, before all else.

Seicho-no-Ie.note: Reconciliation with all things; gratitude to ancestors. The English wording of the Grand Harmony message is not to be quoted yet.

Hinduism.note: A right to the work, not to its fruits.

Christianity.note: Done in secret, not for show.

Hinduism.note: From darkness lead me to light.

Seicho-no-Ie.note: The person as a child of God. UPL credits the phrase and keeps its own (decision D1).

Judaism.note: Humankind in the image of God. The verse does not say what the image is; the mystical teaching of divine sparks is not recorded here and is to be described, not absorbed.

soul.label: The immortal soul (also spirit, consciousness of the person, true self)

Seicho-no-Ie.note: Man is not matter but spiritual existence.

Buddhism.note: Nothing in body or mind is a permanent, unchanging self. UPL parts from Buddhism here and says so (decision D3).

Seicho-no-Ie.note: The silkworm and the cocoon, from the Nectarean Shower of Holy Doctrines.

Hinduism.note: One's own dharma is bound to the four classes in the text. UPL takes the path of right action and not the assignment by birth.

Buddhism.note: In Buddhism the dharma is the teaching and the truth it points to. The same word, a different sense.

Christianity.note: The passage on the least of these ends in eternal punishment, which UPL does not teach.
The Lord's Prayer, without the later doxology.
Allegorical reading: one major strand, and Augustine warns against it as well as for it.

Hinduism.note: The Upanishads teach by dialogue, a teacher answering a student.

Sikhism.note: No intoxicant, in the Sikh code of conduct.

Judaism.note: Saving a life comes before almost every other duty.

Christianity.note: Healing with a word, read as teaching about faith and not as a technique.

Seicho-no-Ie.note: In the True Image there is no disease. UPL holds that illness is real and is treated (decisions D1 and D2).

Hawaiian tradition.note: To set right: a family process led by a respected mediator. The four-phrase form is a modern adaptation.

findings.note: Resolved 21 September 2026 by decision D2 and proposals P1 and P2: the introduction now says "trust in science and modern medicine", and the page states that UPL heals the spirit, medicine treats the body, and a follower never relies on spiritual or alternative remedies alone.

Resolved 21 September 2026 by decision D1 and proposals P4 to P9: God is not a person but the source of light. Comparative Analysis and the God page now say so, "God's love" is explained as the nature of the light, "divine will" became "divine order", and prayer is attunement. Unity still describes Tawhid in Islam's own terms, which is a description of Islam and not of UPL's God.

Resolved 21 September 2026 by decision D3 and proposal P3: Comparative Analysis now honours the Buddha's teaching that suffering can be understood and ended, and states openly that UPL parts from Buddhism on the self.

Two statements of the mission. Name, Mission, and Vision names compassion, wisdom and enlightenment through unity, ethical living and continuous learning; Purpose says the mission "pivots around" freedom, acceptance, ethical living, love and continuous spiritual growth.
The core belief and the practice section carry almost the same title and do not link to each other. A reader or a search engine cannot tell which is the statement and which the elaboration.
The core belief and the way-of-life section share a name and do not link to each other.

Resolved 21 September 2026 by proposal P24. The core belief now states the concept in general, "nothing in existence stands alone, and… to learn is to discover how things are joined", and credits the Huayan school and Thich Nhat Hanh for it. The environmental page remains its application to nature.
Other Practices is a general statement about practice, which the part introduction already gives. Its title promises a list it does not contain.

The silkworm and cocoon image is given in full on both pages, a result of splitting the paper. The image is now credited on The Immortal Soul to Taniguchi's Nectarean Shower of Holy Doctrines (source S07).
Ummah is explained on both pages.
Zakat is explained on both pages.
Tawhid is explained on the first two pages and named again on the third.
Both pages have a subsection on rituals and celebrations. They do not disagree, but neither points to the other, and no page lists the observances.
Both pages define gratitude as a spiritual discipline in similar words.
Ho'oponopono is glossed as reconciliation and forgiveness on both pages.
Both section introductions end on the same phrase, "the soul's progression towards enlightenment and unity with the divine". Found by the wording check, not by reading.
The section introduction lists the four sources of ethics that the page under it then treats one by one.
findings.reason: An introduction that previews its section. Keep the two lists in step.

findings.note: The home page, the Abstract and the Conclusion each summarise the whole. The home page's first sentence repeats the Abstract's.
findings.reason: These are the summary pages of the founding paper. A change of doctrine must be carried into all three.

findings.note: The site configuration holds its own one-paragraph summary of the religion, used in llms.txt and structured data. It is a description, not a teaching, but it is doctrine-shaped text outside content/ and can drift from it.
findings.reason: Machine-facing metadata, allowed by locked decision 3. Re-read it whenever the home page or the Abstract changes.

findings.note: Resolved 21 September 2026 by proposal P21. Both pages gave Seicho-No-Ie's teaching on the child of God in nearly the same words. The God page now says "a being of spirit and not of matter", and "already perfect" stays with belief 4, where it is about innate goodness.
